subject: Mode selection: hosted vs dedicated vs private — next steps & migration checkpoints
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@prioryhealth.com>

Cc: Samuel Ortega <samuel.ortega@prioryhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / demo follow-up — hosting & migration questions

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the demo today — appreciate the clear breakdown of hosting options. A few follow-ups from our side as we start to map internal requirements to Redwood offerings:

- Compliance/regulatory: Priory handles PHI; SOC 2 Type II and a requirement for customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) are non-negotiable.
- Connectivity: we need to understand VPC peering options, egress controls, and whether private endpoints with static IPs are available.
- Migration origin: currently running an internal LLM service on a legacy GPU cluster (NVIDIA V100 pools) with a small self-hosted model as fallback. We also have traffic routed through another public LLM API for edge cases.
- Load profile (very preliminary): daytime peak ~120 requests/sec for classification endpoints, average latency target <200ms p50, bursts up to 250 req/s.
- Data handling: logs must be retained for 90 days and accessible for audits; can’t have unfiltered logging of full inputs in hosted environments unless encrypted.

Attached the security questionnaire and a draft SOW template — please have your security and solutions engineers review. Primary ask: is a Dedicated deployment necessary for our PHI use-case, or can Private (VPC) be a better long-term fit? Also interested in a proposed migration checklist and an estimate for the earliest possible PoC start date.

Thanks,
Sarah Li
Head of Engineering — Data Platform
Priory Health

Subject: Re: Intro / demo follow-up — hosting & migration questions

Sarah — thanks for the follow-up and for sharing the questionnaire and SOW draft. Short answer up-front: given PHI and your audit/KMS requirements, Private (VPC) or Private-on-prem are the safest long-term options; Dedicated can be a practical intermediary if you want faster time-to-PoC with reserved capacity and isolated hardware. Below I laid out pros/cons and an actionable next-step plan so we can scope a POC.

Quick comparison (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to start, minimal ops. Not recommended for PHI unless additional encryption & contract amendments are acceptable.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools under your tenancy with isolated runtime. Gives predictable throughput and faster cutover from other hosted APIs; supports KMS integration and VPC egress. Good for multi-week POC.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full control over network, keys, and audit logs. Best for long-term PHI workloads; longer lead time for setup and network approvals.

Migration notes (from the origins you described):
- From other LLM APIs: mostly data-level work — prompt pairing, prompt templates, tokenization differences. Expect some re-tuning for temperature/top-p to match behavior. No infra-level migration required for this path.
- From self-hosted / legacy GPU clusters: model artifacts (weights, tokenizer) may need conversion depending on format; we’ll validate architecture (Flax/TF/PyTorch) and check quantization/FP16 compatibility. KV cache behavior differs across runtimes; we’ll validate session caching and warm-up strategy.
- From hybrid (self-hosted + public API): recommend a phased route — replicate critical endpoints on Dedicated for parity testing, then cut traffic gradually and run A/B comparisons.

Concrete next steps I propose:
1) Redwood to review security-questionnaire.xlsx (Marcus will own) and return completed sections within 3 business days.
2) Customer to confirm expected sustained QPS, p50/p95 latency goals, and token/day targets. (Sarah — your initial numbers are a good start; can you confirm concurrency requirements?)
3) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with Marcus (solutions) + Monica (eng/CS) to walk network/VPC peering, KMS/HSM options, and initial SRE runbook.
4) If agreed, plan a 4-week Dedicated PoC: configuration recommendation below — 2x A100-equivalent GPUs, 256GB RAM, 2 TB model cache to start; can scale up after benchmark runs.

I attached a Redwood migration checklist (redwood-migration-checklist.xlsx) with typical touchpoints and a suggested timeline. I’ve cc’d Monica and Marcus to coordinate. When you confirm a 2-hour window for the technical call I’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,

Ava, Monica —
Couple quick clarifications before we lock call times:

- SOC 2: must be Type II — do you have a current report we can review?
- HSM/KMS: we require customer-managed keys with a BYOK flow. Can Redwood support Cloud HSM (GCP) or our on-prem HSM via key wrapping?

Sam / Sarah — thanks for the quick clarifications. Quick answers below and proposed timeline so we can get the PoC scheduled: 

- SOC 2 Type II: we can share the latest report under NDA; Marcus will attach the document during the technical call if needed.
- KMS/HSM/BYOK: Redwood supports customer-managed keys in both Dedicated and Private modes. For GCP Cloud HSM we support direct KMS integration; for on-prem HSMs we offer a key-wrapping flow and can coordinate with your security team on key rotation policy.
- Maintenance windows & SLA: we offer configurable blackout windows for Dedicated and Private customers; standard maintenance notices are 72 hours in advance for non-critical patches, emergency patches follow the SLA playbook. We’ll include proposed blackout times in the runbook.
- Static egress IPs: yes — Dedicated and Private support fixed egress addresses for allow-listing.

POC proposal (timeline & scope):
- Week 0: sign SOW and security access (NDA already in progress)
- Week 1: Dedicated environment provisioning + network peering setup (VPC peering and firewall allow-listing)
- Week 2: Model import + baseline benchmarking; initial tuning for parity with your current model behavior
- Week 3: Load tests and A/B traffic split (10% traffic)
- Week 4: Final checklist, SLO verification, and cutover planning

Deliverables: provisioning guide, runbook (includes blackout windows & rotation), completed security questionnaire, and a final sizing report.

Action items: Monica — can you own the runbook draft and network play (target EOD Thurs)? Marcus — please prepare SOC2 artifact list and KMS flow diagram for the call. Sarah / Sam — if you can share the concurrency/token forecast by EOD, I’ll lock a technical deep-dive for next Tue (60 minutes).
